title: Someone Scraped 5.6 Billion TikTok Videos and Put the Data on Hugging Face for Free
key_facts: A developer called hashfunction posted metadata for about 5.6 billion public TikTok videos on Hugging Face, free to download.
It is metadata, not video: captions, hashtags, sound IDs, view and like counts; 460 GB of Parquet files.
It is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0, free for research and personal use; commercial use is routed to datasocial.ai and the scraper code is sold separately for $1,699.
DataSocial's own write-up describes reaching TikTok's private mobile API with generated device identities and spoofed requests.
TikTok's US terms bar automated extraction without written approval; its official Research Tools are limited to qualifying researchers.
quote_evidence: A developer who goes by hashfunction has posted metadata for about 5.6 billion public TikTok videos on the open-source AI repository Hugging Face, free to download.
Section 3.4 of TikTok's U.S. terms of service bars extracting data from the platform with automated software unless TikTok approves it in writing.
why_it_matters_hint: AI developers want such data and TikTok limits access, so the release raises terms-of-service and legal questions.
notes: No TikTok response reported in the article. The scraping method is DataSocial's own description.
